title: What Merton gives
hookLine: holiness is becoming who you truly are before God

lines: A STATUE WITH A FARAWAY LOOK.
cards: When people hear the word saint, they often picture someone who isn't quite human: a statue with a halo and a blank, faraway look. Perfect, and a little boring. And they think: that's not me.
I'm too messy, too loud, too ordinary. Merton had a different picture. After the restlessness, the monastery, the books, the woods and the long trip east, he left one idea people keep coming back to.
Holiness isn't becoming someone else. Today: true self.

teach.h: TO BE A SAINT IS TO BE MYSELF.
teach.b: First, the idea. In New Seeds of Contemplation, Merton wrote that for him, to be a saint means to be himself. Not a copy of someone else's holiness.
The real person God had in mind. He said a tree gives glory to God by being a tree, fully, and not trying to be something else. Second, the root.
This isn't self-help. For Merton, your true self isn't something you invent. It's who God knows you to be.
The prophet Jeremiah hears God say, in the Douay-Rheims: "Before I formed thee in the bowels of thy mother, I knew thee." The prophet is known before he has done anything.
For Merton, holiness is growing into being known like that, the way a seed grows into the tree it already is. Third, the road we've walked.
Look back at these eighteen days. Inquietum, orphaned and drifting. A convert drawn in New York.
A Trappist in the silence. A mountain climbed one ledge at a time. Vigils before dawn.
Waking up. The false self and the true. Seeds everywhere.
Strangers shining on a street corner. Not knowing the road. A hermit in the woods.
A monk speaking about war and race, making friends across traditions, alone for others. A clear morning in Sri Lanka, and a sudden end in Bangkok. That's not a perfect life.
It's a real one, becoming itself before God. Fourth, what he gives.

teach.h: BEFORE I FORMED THEE, I KNEW THEE.
teach.b: Permission to be restless, to ask questions, to not know, to love people who differ from you, to keep changing. And, underneath, his conviction that the person God made you to be is worth becoming.

how: Catholics believe every person is called to holiness, a teaching the Second Vatican Council called the universal call to holiness, and many read Merton, the saints and scripture to discover their own particular path.

o: the private self you hide from God and others
the real you God already knows, not a copy of anyone
the confident image you show to other people

games.q: you feel too messy and ordinary to be holy. what does Merton's picture of a saint say to you?
o: become who you truly are before God
games.why: for Merton, to be a saint is to be yourself: the person God knew before you were formed.

practice: Think of one thing that's truly you, a way you laugh, a thing you love, a kindness only you seem to do: not the polished version, the real one.
Be glad of it for a moment without comparing it to anyone, then imagine offering it back, a gift always meant to be given. If you pray, thank God for making you you.

wordCard.voice: True self, Merton's conviction that holiness means becoming the real person God already knows, not a copy of anyone else's. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: become who you are. That closes the days with Merton. Tomorrow, the map of the Catholic faith.
